_about: v5.00 swap, the staffing flip (stream h, 2026-11-24). The rulebook text that becomes true when the two held flip records apply at the switch: sql/2026-11-24-s2-staff-powers-v463.sql and sql/2026-11-24-s2-all-staff-voting-v463.sql (branch db/s2-committees). Applied ONLY in the flip commit, by tools/s2-rulebook-splice.cjs; never commit the spliced src/live/part3_content.js before then.

The rulings (league law): no departments in Season 2, one staff group (commissioner, 2026-10-19 and 2026-11-23); every staff member and commissioner votes on owner, staff and front-office applications, 50% + 1, banned and staff-suspended members excluded (2026-11-23, main session 2026-11-24); only committee managers or commissioners suspend, up to 14 days or 18 games in steps of three, anything longer applied for and approved by a commissioner, other staff file requests, bans commissioner only (2026-11-23); one staff notifications channel, and bans, unbans and lifts get a notice (2026-11-23); the Draft and Bidding manager runs bidding and the draft room tools (2026-11-23).

Each edit anchors on an exact substring of one section field (paragraphs or full): it must match exactly once in that field, or the splice stops. An edit already applied (its new text present once, its old text gone) is skipped, so the splice is idempotent. Edits that change a sentence another test pins are listed in the stream h report with the assertion lines to update in the same commit.

Readings that the database drafts enforce but the commissioner has not ruled in words, written here because the book must say what the site enforces: any staff member may give a formal warning; a committee manager or a commissioner decides an appeal and lifts a suspension. Each is listed in the report as open with the commissioner.

edits.old: A complaint is routed to the department that must act on it, and that department is notified the moment one is filed: complaints about conduct on the ice go to the officiating department, and complaints about conduct in the Discord go to the community department. Appeals go to the department that decides the conduct appealed (Rule 7.6). Both departments issue warnings and suspensions within the ceilings of Rule 7.2 and escalate anything heavier. A department rules on the conduct it sees: the officiating department is not asked to decide a chat matter it never read, and the community department is not asked to decide a hit it never watched.
edits.new: A complaint is filed under the conduct it concerns, conduct on the ice or conduct in the Discord, and every member of league staff is notified the moment one is filed. Appeals are decided under Rule 7.6. Any member of league staff may give a formal warning; a committee manager or a commissioner suspends within the limits of Rule 7.2, and any other member of league staff who finds a suspension warranted files a suspension request under that rule.

edits.old: League staff (the officiating and community departments) suspend a rostered member for a number of games in steps of three (3), from three (3) to eighteen (18) games, and suspend a member who holds no roster spot to a date no more than thirty (30) days away. A longer suspension, a suspension for the remainder of the season other than under paragraph 4 or paragraph 7 of this rule, an expulsion, and any sanction against a commissioner or a member of league staff are imposed only by a commissioner; a staff official who believes a case warrants more leaves it open and escalates it.
edits.new: Any member of league staff may issue a formal warning. Only a committee manager (Rule S2.8) or a commissioner may issue a suspension. A committee manager suspends a rostered member for a number of games in steps of three (3), from three (3) to eighteen (18) games, and a member who holds no roster spot to a date no more than fourteen (14) days from the start of the suspension. A longer suspension, and any suspension for the remainder of a season other than under paragraph 7 of this rule, is imposed by a commissioner, or is applied for by a suspension request and takes effect only when a commissioner approves it. An expulsion, and any sanction against a commissioner or a member of league staff, are imposed only by a commissioner. A member of league staff who is not a committee manager and believes a case warrants a suspension files a suspension request stating its grounds. A committee manager or a commissioner decides a request within the limits of this paragraph, save that a committee manager does not decide a request they filed or one about themselves; only a commissioner decides a request beyond those limits or one about a commissioner or a member of league staff. An approved request imposes exactly the suspension approved, and a request is denied only with a reason, which the member of staff who filed it is told.

edits.old: Further misconduct while a suspension runs is dealt with by extending it: staff add games in steps of three (3), to a total of eighteen (18), or add days to a suspension to a date, within the ceilings of paragraph 1 of this rule.
edits.new: Further misconduct while a suspension runs is dealt with by extending it, in the suspension's own terms: games added in steps of three (3) to a suspension counted in games, or a later last day for a suspension to a date. A committee manager may extend a suspension to a total of eighteen (18) games, or to a last day no more than fourteen (14) days from the day the suspension was issued; an extension past those limits is made only by a commissioner. A suspension request filed against a member who is serving a suspension is a request to extend it: it states in writing why the suspension should be extended, the member is told that reason, and its approval extends the running suspension by exactly the games or days approved. A committee manager may approve such a request only within those limits; past them, only a commissioner may. A member serving a suspension for the remainder of a season has none to extend, and a commissioner rules on further misconduct.

edits.old: A community suspension of a rostered member runs three (3) to eighteen (18) games in steps of three (3). A member who holds no roster spot is suspended to a date no more than thirty (30) days away and, while the suspension runs, is also placed in a timeout in the league Discord until 11:59 PM Eastern Time on its last day. The department chooses the length on the seriousness of the conduct, its effect on the member or members subjected to it, and the member's history under this rule (Rule 7.5). A suspension longer than eighteen (18) games, an expulsion from the league, and any sanction against a commissioner or a member of league staff are imposed only by a commissioner; the department that wants one leaves the case open and refers it to the league office with what it has found.
edits.new: A suspension under this rule is imposed as Rule 7.2 provides: a committee manager suspends a rostered member for three (3) to eighteen (18) games in steps of three (3), and a member who holds no roster spot to a date no more than fourteen (14) days from the start of the suspension. A member who holds no roster spot is also placed, while the suspension runs, in a timeout in the league Discord until 11:59 PM Eastern Time on its last day. The official imposing the suspension chooses its length on the seriousness of the conduct, its effect on the member or members subjected to it, and the member's history under this rule (Rule 7.5). A longer suspension, and any suspension for the remainder of a season, takes effect only when a commissioner approves it (Rule 7.2); an expulsion from the league, and any sanction against a commissioner or a member of league staff, are imposed only by a commissioner, and a member of league staff who believes one is warranted leaves the case open and refers it to the league office with what they have found.

changelogDraft.summary: The league staff is one group with no departments: committee managers and commissioners suspend, and every staff member and commissioner votes on applications
items: Season 2 has no staff departments: every member of league staff may do the work of any committee, and every automated staff notice goes to one staff channel (Rule S2.8).
Every member of league staff and every commissioner votes on owner, staff, General Manager and Assistant General Manager applications; more than half of all of them decides one (Rule 2.6).

Only a committee manager or a commissioner suspends: up to eighteen (18) games in steps of three, or to a date up to fourteen (14) days away. Anything longer is applied for and a commissioner approves it; other staff file a suspension request (Rules 7.2 and 7.7).
A committee manager or a commissioner decides an appeal; an appeal by or about a member of league staff or a commissioner is decided only by a commissioner (Rule 7.6).

A suspension request against a member already serving a suspension asks to extend it, in its own terms and with a written reason; an approved request imposes exactly what was approved, and a committee manager's second suspension of a member in a season is either kept within their limits or sent to a commissioner for the rest of the season (Rule 7.2).
Trades, reschedules, voids, disconnection counts and statistics corrections go to the league staff rather than a department (Rules 2.1, 2.3, 3.2, 3.3, 4.2, 4.3 and 6.3).
